title: Data residency: choose the agency's data region at creation
goal: Let the platform place an agency's database and files in a chosen region, such as the EU.
why: R2 is pinned to APAC and D1 has no location hint (terraform/modules/cloudflare/workers.tf); EU buyers ask where data lives.
blockedOnOwner: owner decision Q7 (which regions at launch)
steps: regions.ts: Region = in|eu|uk|us|au|gulf -> { d1: { locationHint?, jurisdiction? }, r2Binding } per READINESS-PLAN 4.12 (eu/uk -> jurisdiction eu, FILE_STORAGE_EU; others -> FILE_STORAGE with hint).

Master 0022: tenants.region already added in R104 (0012); this migration adds region-related columns only if needed (e.g. files_bucket) or is a no-op comment file; skip creating it if nothing is needed and say so.

Provisioners pass the D1 options; files routes and every R2 access pick the binding via getFileStorage(env, tenant) (grep FILE_STORAGE in backend/src); gen-wrangler and base config declare FILE_STORAGE_EU; terraform creates travelcrm-files-eu with jurisdiction eu.
Super admin wizard region select is in R112's wizard (backend accepts region already); if the console lacks the field, add it as a follow-up request.
tests: backend/test/data-residency.test.ts: an eu tenant's uploads go to FILE_STORAGE_EU (local binding) and an in tenant's to FILE_STORAGE; the Cloudflare provisioner sends jurisdiction eu for eu and a location hint for us (mocked fetch).
acceptance: Region respected for DB creation and every file read/write (tests).
gate: cd backend && npx vitest run   # pass: 0 failed files and passed >= the last merged count (1296 on 2026-10-14)
goLiveVerify: D1 jurisdiction support in the REST create call; EU R2 bucket; privacy policy states that master data (agency names, user emails, usage) is global.
notes: Before editing read: this batch file, docs/readiness/READINESS-PLAN.md sections 0 and the design note for this area, desktop/audit/fix/FIX-PLAN.md sections 3-4 (executor rules, worktree bootstrap with node_modules junctions; never npm install inside a worktree unless the batch adds a dependency, and then only in the main checkout by the orchestrator).

Backend tests follow the existing pattern (see backend/test/voip-callbacks.test.ts): import env, createExecutionContext, waitOnExecutionContext, applyD1Migrations from cloudflare:test; applyD1Migrations(env.MASTER_DB, env.TEST_MIGRATIONS) in beforeAll; POST /api/v1/test/reset; call worker.fetch(request, env, ctx). isolatedStorage is false and singleWorker true, so use unique ids/emails per test file.
Add FILE_STORAGE_EU to the vitest wrangler config through wrangler.base.toml/wrangler.toml so tests get a local bucket.
